plan.topic: ADR-0003: Render Mermaid diagrams client-side instead of at build time
plan.title: ADR-0003: Rendering Mermaid Diagrams for a Live Theme Toggle
plan.throughLine: Because the docs site's dark-mode toggle can flip at any moment, Mermaid diagrams must be able to react live — which pushes rendering from build time into the browser, and shapes every detail of how the component is built.

beats.title: The clash between static rendering and a live toggle
beats.intent: Establish why this decision exists: the site needs Mermaid diagrams and dark mode together, but Mermaid only renders one theme at a time, and a reader can flip themes without reloading. Frame the build-time-vs-client-side question this creates.

beats.title: Weighing the options, landing on mermaid.render()
beats.intent: Walk through the three real options considered — build-time rehype-mermaid with its Chromium/CI cost and dual-SVG swapping, client-side mermaid.run() which destroys the source text needed for re-rendering, and client-side mermaid.render() which preserves source in a data-attribute and re-renders on a MutationObserver watching Starlight's data-theme attribute — and state the decision made.

beats.title: Living with the trade-offs
beats.intent: Cover what accepting this decision costs and gains: a brief unstyled flash and a JS requirement (mitigated with role=img and fallback text), a faster/simpler build pipeline, the gotcha that diagram source must come via a code prop rather than MDX slot content, and the acknowledged condition — rising no-JS readership — that would justify revisiting toward build-time rendering.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Welcome back — today we're digging into ADR-0003, which is all about rendering Mermaid diagrams on a site that also has to support dark mode. The tricky part is that Mermaid only knows how to render one theme at a time, but our readers can flip that dark mode toggle whenever they feel like it, no page reload required.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Right, and that mismatch is really the whole story here. If you bake the diagrams into SVG at build time, you get a fast page with zero rendering JavaScript shipped to the browser, but you're locking in one theme forever. So the question the team had to answer was blunt: do we pre-render for speed, or render client-side so the diagrams can actually react live to that toggle?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So walk me through the actual options on the table. Where did the team start looking?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: First was build-time rendering with rehype-mermaid, which is great because it ships zero client JS and even works without JavaScript enabled. But rehype-mermaid drives a headless Chromium during astro build — so now every contributor and every CI run needs that dependency. Then there's client-side rendering with mermaid dot run, Mermaid's own DOM-scanning API, which is simple to wire up but replaces the diagram element's content in place — once it consumes the source text to draw the diagram, that text is gone, so re-rendering later for a theme change has nothing to work from.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So neither of those actually solves the re-render problem. What was the third option?

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: mermaid dot render, called with an id and the source text, which lets you keep the original source in a data- attribute on the container so it survives the render instead of being consumed. Pair that with a MutationObserver watching html's data-theme attribute — the same attribute Starlight's toggle already sets — and a theme flip just triggers a re-render from that stored source. That's what got implemented in Mermaid.astro: render once on load, then re-render live on any theme change, no duplicate build artifacts.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So what's the actual cost of living with this? I imagine there's a flash before the diagram renders, and presumably it just doesn't work without JavaScript at all.

turns.speaker: guest
turns.text: Right on both counts — you get a brief flash of the raw pre fallback before Mermaid hydrates, and no JS means no diagram, full stop, so we added role=img plus that visible fallback text to keep it accessible rather than just broken. In exchange the build pipeline stays fast with no headless browser to flake in CI, and there's one sharp gotcha we documented right in the component: diagram source has to come in as a code prop from a .mmd file, not slot content, because MDX mangles whitespace-sensitive syntax. If analytics ever show a real chunk of no-JS readers, that's the trigger to revisit toward build-time SVG pairs, but for now this is accepted and shipped in Mermaid.astro.
